subject: Execution geography and erasure boundaries — ACME Health follow-up
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:02:00+01:00
Subject: Execution geography and deletion SLA questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A couple of questions came up from our security and procurement teams that we need clarified before we move to procurement: where exactly are inference requests for ACME Health processed, and which subprocessors could touch payloads during processing? We have a strict EU-first requirement — ideally no processing outside the EU unless under SCCs and explicit exception.

Specifically:
- Can you list the regions (cloud regions) where requests may execute for the Hosted API and for Dedicated?
- Which subprocessors are involved (for routing, storage, telemetry, etc.) and their locations?
- For cross-border handoffs, what contractual / technical controls (SCCs, encryption-in-transit, KMS residency) do you provide?
- If a customer requests deletion of all ACME data, what are the expected timelines (token cache, logs, backups) and the mechanics (API + manual confirm)?

If it helps, I can share our intake form. We need this to feed into legal.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Security
ACME Health

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:18:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Execution geography and deletion SLA questions

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short overview (attached) and summarized the answers below to accelerate your legal review. Attaching: Redwood-Data-Processing-Overview.pdf (summary + subprocessors list).

Short answers (high-level):
- Regions: Hosted API defaults to EU regions for EU-tenant traffic (primary: eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). Requests may be routed to additional EU/nearby regions for capacity; we do not route EU-tenant traffic to non-EU regions unless a customer explicitly enables cross-region failover.
- Dedicated: With Dedicated capacity, you can provision GPU pools in a single EU region (we support private subnets in eu-west-1, eu-central-1, and eu-north-1).
- Subprocessors: Core subprocessors are listed in the attached doc. For inference serving and orchestration we use Redwood-managed clusters (own runtime + delivery infra), cloud provider compute (AWS/OCI/Google) in the region you select, and a small set of telemetry/monitoring partners (PagerDuty, Datadog) — telemetry retention is minimal and scrubbed of PII. For any non-EU subprocessors we provide documented justifications and SCCs where applicable.
- Controls: We support customer KMS key integration (bring-your-own-key) so that model payloads can be encrypted at rest with a key you control. All inter-service traffic is TLS 1.2/1.3; internal links use mTLS. Cross-border transfers rely on SCCs + documented subprocessors; we are prepared to provide a processor-addendum and SCC exhibit for your legal team.
- Deletion: API-driven delete requests will evict token-KV caches within minutes depending on load. Indexed logs (for troubleshooting) are purged per retention policy — default 90 days, configurable down to 30 days for enterprise customers. Backups: immutable backups are retained per policy and deleted on a best-effort schedule; we provide an erasure confirmation once deletion workflows complete. For Dedicated/private installs we can provide shorter timelines via contract.

Next steps: Rishi has more technical detail on subprocessors and exact deletion flows (what gets scrubbed, what remains for audit logs). Rishi, can you add the routing table and the specific subprocessor-country map for EU tenants? Ben — flag anything I missed re: contractual exhibits.

Best,
Olga
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Data-Processing-Overview.pdf (summary + named subprocessors and locations)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmehealth.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:37:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Execution geography and deletion SLA questions

On 02/12/2026 09:18, Olga Petrov wrote:
> - Regions: Hosted API defaults to EU regions for EU-tenant traffic (primary: eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). Requests may be routed to additional EU/nearby regions for capacity; we do not route EU-tenant traffic to non-EU regions unless a customer explicitly enables cross-region failover.

Hi Samira — quick technical addendum to clarify the behaviors and timelines.

1) Routing & failover
- Policy: We tag tenant traffic by tenancy metadata at the edge. For EU-tagged tenants, routing policy first selects EU-prefixed endpoints. Only if those endpoints are saturated AND you’ve opted into cross-region failover (explicit toggle) will requests be routed outside the EU. We can ship a policy that disables failover for ACME by default.

2) Subprocessor map (short):
- Compute: AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland), GCP europe-west2 (London), Azure westeurope (Netherlands) — compute runs in the region you select.
- Object storage: Customer data-at-rest may be stored in region-backed object stores; snapshot replication is disabled for EU-tenants unless explicitly enabled.
- Telemetry/observability: Datadog (EU-hosted project) for metrics; PagerDuty (global) for alerting — alert payloads exclude raw prompts.
- Support & logs: Support engineers may access anonymized traces via our console; access is logged and gated by ACLs and customer opt-in.

3) Deletion mechanics & SLAs
- Token/KV cache: eviction within 1–10 minutes after API delete call (depends on cache TTL and active sessions).
- Indexed logs & observability: configurable retention; we propose 30 days (minimum) for ACME by contract.
- Backups / snapshots: immutable backups have a longer retention window (configurable). Deletion from backups is a best-effort process: typically completed within 7–30 days depending on the backup schedule. We provide a signed erasure confirmation once objects are removed from live stores and snapshots are rotated and expired.
- Audit trail: Deletion actions are logged to an audit ledger (read-only) for compliance; entries show the deletion request and job id but do not retain deleted payload content.

4) Transfer controls
- SCCs: we provide standard EU SCC exhibits and are open to executing client-supplied SCCs as an exhibit to the PSA.
- Encryption: TLS in transit; AES-256 at rest. We support customer-managed KMS keys (HSM-backed) — key location can be EU-only if required.

5) Private/Dedicated option
- For customers with strict residency requirements, Dedicated or Private deployments can be pinned to a single region and restricted to customer VPCs. In that model, subprocessors are reduced (we can exclude certain telemetry partners).

I can attach a CSV with the full subprocessor-country mapping if that helps for legal.

Cheers,
Rishi
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups so we can close the loop with procurement/legal: 

- Please attach the full CSV subprocessor-country map and the Redwood SCC exhibit. We also need explicit language on whether any telemetry partner will store excerpted prompt text outside the EU (our policy forbids that).
- Confirm the minimum contractual deletion SLA you can commit to for indexed logs and backups (we need committed numbers for contract: e.g., token eviction in X mins, log purge in Y days, backups scrubbed within Z days).
- We would like a short statement from your security team confirming that support access to traces is on a need-to-know basis and that traces do not contain raw prompts.

Can you put these in a short attachment so legal can insert directly into the DPA? Also copying Jorge from procurement — he may request pricing for Dedicated in eu-central-1 if we need a hard residency contract.

If you can send the CSV + exhibits by EOD tomorrow that would be ideal.

Best,
Samira
